message.content:
Below is a concise list of the **long‑weekend holidays that apply nationwide in Canada for 2023** (i.e., federal holidays that either fall on a weekend or are observed on the nearest weekday).  
For a complete, province‑specific list you’ll need to add the provincial holidays that create additional long weekends (e.g., Family Day in Alberta, British Columbia, etc.).

| Date(s) | Holiday | Notes |
|---------|---------|-------|
| **Jan 2 – Jan 4** | New Year’s Day (observed) | New Year’s Day fell on Sunday, Jan 1, so it was observed on Monday, Jan 2. The weekend (Jan 1–2) plus the observed day creates a long weekend. |
| **Jul 3 – Jul 5** | Canada Day (observed) | Canada Day fell on Saturday, Jul 1, so it was observed on Monday, Jul 3. The weekend (Jul 1–2) plus the observed day creates a long weekend. |
| **Nov 13 – Nov 15** | Remembrance Day (observed) | Remembrance Day fell on Saturday, Nov 11, so it was observed on Monday, Nov 13. The weekend (Nov 11–12) plus the observed day creates a long weekend. |

### How to use this in your app

If you want to programmatically generate the long‑weekend periods, you can store the above data in a JSON array:

```json
[
  {
    "start": "2023-01-02",
    "end": "2023-01-04",
    "holiday": "New Year's Day (observed)"
  },
  {
    "start": "2023-07-03",
    "end": "2023-07-05",
    "holiday": "Canada Day (observed)"
  },
  {
    "start": "2023-11-13",
    "end": "2023-11-15",
    "holiday": "Remembrance Day (observed)"
  }
]
```

You can then feed this array into your holiday‑planning logic to highlight or filter long weekends. If you need province‑specific holidays, you’ll have to merge this list with the respective provincial holiday calendars.
